name: Squamate Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro to northeastern rio grande do sul)
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed antbird found on the ground in humid forests. Both sexes have rufous-brown crown, back, and tail and a buff vent.

name: Tabora Cisticola
rangeDescription: Southeastern uganda to southwestern kenya, rwanda, tanzania, southeastern democratic republic of the congo, and zambia
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed, plain cisticola. Note the rufous cap and the white tip to the tail.

name: Hispaniolan Parakeet
rangeDescription: Hispaniola
description: A sleek, medium-large, gregarious species of woodlands that sometimes ventures into agricultural and urban areas. Its overall green plumage, long, pointed tail, and stout bill eliminate all other species in range.

name: Thick-billed Berrypecker
rangeDescription: New guinea (mountains of bird's head peninsula and central highlands)
description: A small, rare bird of mid-montane forest. Male is dark gray above and pale gray below with a slight, pale tuft on the side.

name: Yapacana Antbird
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern colombia, southwestern venezuela, and northwestern brazil (amazonas)
description: Odd, slender antbird with a rather long bill. Males are gray above and white below with white spots on the wings; females have rusty underparts and lack wing spots.

name: Yellow-eyed Black-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern democratic republic of the congo to rwanda, burundi, and southwestern uganda
description: Slim, long-tailed, all-black flycatcher with a pale yellow eye. Found along the edge and in clearings within Albertine Rift montane forest.

name: Biak Megapode
rangeDescription: Islands in cenderawasih bay (off northwestern new guinea)
description: A small, dark scrubfowl of forest and disturbed habitats on the Bay Islands where the only member of its family. Sooty gray plumage, bare red to gray face, slight crest at the back of the head, reddish legs, and yellowish bill.

name: Wied's Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southern bahia, espírito santo, and minas gerais)
description: Nondescript manakin that may be mistaken for a flycatcher. Has an olive-green back, a grayish throat, and yellowish underparts.

name: Black-chested Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid highlands of southwestern mexico (jalisco to western oaxaca)
description: Very handsome but rather local sparrow endemic to interior southwest Mexico. Found in scrubby woodland and edge of dry tropical foothills and interior valleys.

name: Spix's Macaw
rangeDescription: Palm groves of northeastern brazil (northern bahia); on verge of extinction
description: Now declared extinct in the wild; only a few individuals survive in captivity. Medium-sized macaw with grayish head shading to deep glaucous blue in the rest of the plumage, contrasting with the black sturdy bill.

name: Chico's Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: South-central amazonian brazil (between the rio madeira and rio aripuanã)
description: Recently-described flycatcher of short-stature Amazonian white sand forests. Has green-olive upperparts and yellow underparts.

name: Common Bronzewing
rangeDescription: Australia including tasmania
description: A plump, attractive brown pigeon with beautiful green and bronze iridescent coloration in the wings. Males have a bright yellow and white forehead that is absent in females.

name: Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (mindoro)
description: A small bird of lowland and foothill forest and more open wooded areas on Mindoro, slightly glossy black with a white belly and sides of the chest and with red patches on the throat, upper back, and in a stripe from the center of the chest down the belly. Note the fairly long, thin, slightly curved bill.

name: Bar-winged Oriole
rangeDescription: Oak-pine scrub of southern mexico (southeastern oaxaca) to el salvador
description: Very local, poorly known black-and-yellow oriole of Chiapas and northern Central America. Favors brushy oak woodlands and semi-deciduous scrubby areas, especially with oaks.

name: Subtropical Pygmy-Owl
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of ecuador, peru, and far northern bolivia
description: Rarely encountered owl found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes. Small with a round head, yellow eyes, white-speckled crown, and white bands on wings and tail.

name: Visayan Shama
rangeDescription: Philippines (ticao, masbate, panay, and negros)
description: A medium-sized, long-tailed bird of lowland and foothill forest in the western Visayas. Black on the upperparts and tail, with a white belly and pale pink legs.

name: Green-backed Tailorbird
rangeDescription: Northern and central luzon (philippines)
description: A small, long-billed, long-tailed bird of dense tangled undergrowth in lowland and foothill forest and bamboo in northern Luzon. Has olive-green wings, back, and tail, a pale gray belly, a gray chest with streaks, a rufous cap reaching below the eye, and orange legs.

name: Dusky-headed Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia (upper magdalena valley)
description: This Colombian endemic has a limited range in the southern Andes, where it can be found in both the eastern and central cordilleras. It has dark upperparts, yellow underparts, and a distinctive black mustache stripe.

name: Great White Pelican
rangeDescription: Locally in south-central eurasia, southern asia, and africa
description: A large white waterbird with a hefty bill and a yellow-orange throat pouch. Note the pink bare skin around eye that extends towards the bill.

name: Nilgiri Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Foothill forest of southwestern peninsular india (mysore southward to kerala)
description: Entirely indigo-blue male is unique; Verditer Flycatcher is brighter blue and more elongated. Female Nilgiri is gray overall, though can sometimes show a bluish tinge in good lighting.
